findings.message: The heading regex `(?m)^#{1,6}[ \t]+(.+?)...$` runs over the whole Markdown text and does not track code fences. A `# comment` line inside a ```python or ```bash block in a doc therefore becomes a heading. That creates a bogus chunk with a selector like `docs/x.md#comment` and cuts the real section's text short at that point. The ticket asks for one chunk per heading, and a line inside a fenced code block is not a heading. The regex also drops a trailing `#` that is part of the heading text, such as `# C#`, which it records as `C`.
findings.paved_road: Walk the text line by line, toggling an in-fence flag on lines whose stripped form starts with ``` (the same check tickets.py and stages.py already use), and treat only out-of-fence ATX lines as headings. Strip a closing `#` run only when whitespace comes before it. Add a unit test with a fenced `# comment` that must not produce a chunk.

findings.message: Criterion 11 requires the source scan to fail on any `os.`, `subprocess`, `time.` or `datetime.now` use. This check only fails on a direct call of the form `os.X(...)`, `subprocess.X(...)` or `time.X(...)`. It still passes for `os.path.exists(p)` (the call's func is a nested Attribute), `os.environ[...]`, `import subprocess` / `from subprocess import run`, `from time import monotonic`, and a `time.monotonic` reference that is never called. For those cases the test cannot fail.
findings.paved_road: Fail on every `ast.Attribute` whose base `ast.Name` is `os`, `subprocess` or `time`, whether or not it is called, and on every `ast.Import`/`ast.ImportFrom` of `os`, `subprocess`, `time` or `datetime`. Alternatively, also assert that the source text contains none of `os.`, `subprocess`, `time.` or `datetime.now`.
